highlights.title: Indeed Hiring Lab: US Labor Market Snapshot — October 2026
highlights.summary: Indeed's monthly US labor market snapshot covering job postings, wages, unemployment, and openings as of October 2026; provides the freshest real-time signal on posting volumes and wage trends across occupations.

highlights.title: The hidden costs of technological change: investigating pathways through which highly automatable jobs undermine workers' health in Germany
highlights.summary: Peer-reviewed study using German panel data finds that workers in highly automatable jobs face measurable health and well-being penalties beyond wage loss, quantifying displacement-adjacent harm pathways for a large employed population.

highlights.title: Artificial Intelligence Policy and Wage Gaps: Evidence from China
highlights.summary: Using panel data for 280 Chinese cities from 2011–2023 and a quasi-natural experiment around AI pilot zone designation, this study estimates AI policy's causal effect on local wage gaps, offering cross-national quantitative evidence on AI-driven wage polarization.

highlights.title: When AI Enters the Workplace, Who Faces Greater Risk? A Gendered Analysis
highlights.summary: AAAI AIES peer-reviewed paper quantifies differential AI displacement risk by gender across occupations, finding women face systematically higher exposure on automatable task bundles and that existing wage gaps compound predicted displacement risk.

highlights.title: AI-driven 'new migrants': skill-spatial mismatch and out-migration intention
highlights.summary: Using China Migrant Population Dynamic Monitoring Survey and patent data across 250 cities (2014–2018), finds AI penetration increases skill-spatial mismatch and raises out-migration intention among lower-skill workers, providing city-level quantitative displacement evidence.

highlights.title: WORKFORCE TRANSFORMATION IN MANUFACTURING INDUSTRIES: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE, AUTOMATION, RESKILLING, UPSKILLING AND SOFT SKILLS
highlights.summary: Reviews empirical evidence on AI and robotics adoption in manufacturing, reporting quantitative estimates of task displacement and reskilling needs across production occupations, relevant to physical automation displacement trends.

highlights.title: The Economic Implications of Artificial Intelligence for Employment and Labour Productivity: A Descriptive Evidence Synthesis (2020–2025)
highlights.summary: Evidence synthesis covering 2020–2025 enterprise AI-adoption statistics and occupational-exposure assessments, synthesizing multiple empirical studies to distinguish technological displacement from productivity augmentation effects on employment.

highlights.title: When Do AI Gains Become Broadly Shareable? A Policy Threshold for AI-Driven Automation
highlights.summary: Extends a standard task-automation growth model with an AI capability parameter to derive a policy stress-test threshold at which automation productivity gains become broadly distributable rather than concentrated, offering a quantitative framework for wage-impact projections.

highlights.title: Chicago Fed Working Papers: Making Sense of Labor-Market Indicators Amid Data Imperfections
highlights.summary: Chicago Fed working paper addresses measurement challenges in current US labor-market indicators, providing methodological context for interpreting displacement and wage signals in an era of rapid structural change.

highlights.title: Chicago Fed Working Papers: The Chicago Fed Labor Market Indicators: Bridging the Gap with Alternative Labor Data
highlights.summary: Chicago Fed working paper introduces a composite labor market indicator reconciling BLS survey data with alternative high-frequency sources, useful for tracking employment shifts in AI-exposed sectors with greater timeliness.

highlights.title: Supporting or Replacing Students' Reasoning? Cognitive Offloading in AI-Assisted Proof Learning
highlights.summary: RCT with 153 undergraduates finds staggered AI chatbot access measurably shifts learning outcomes, providing causal evidence on AI's effect on early-career skill formation and human-capital development relevant to education sector displacement.

themes: Wage polarization and distributional effects of AI automation remain the dominant empirical focus, with China city-level and cross-national studies adding causal identification
Gendered and health-adjacent displacement pathways are gaining peer-reviewed traction, extending displacement evidence beyond headline job-count metrics
Multiple high-value recurring government and institutional data series (BLS OEWS, ACS, RPS GenAI Tracker, Stanford DEL) are overdue for ingest, creating gaps in the prediction graph baselines
